targets.name: Erdos9.erdos_9.variants.infinite
targets.plain: The set is known to be infinite. In [Er77c] Erdős credits Schinzel with proving that there are infinitely many odd integers not of this form, but gives no reference. [Er77c] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III._.

targets.name: Erdos9.erdos_9
targets.plain: Is the upper density of the set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus two powers of 2 positive?

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n1
targets.plain: Every triangle-free graph on 5 vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most 1 edge. This is the n = 1 case of Erdős Problem 23.
targets.statement: : ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)), H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 1

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n5
targets.plain: Every triangle-free graph on 25 vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most 25 edges. This is the n = 5 case of Erdős Problem 23. It follows from the high-density range of Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky together with McKay's complete catalogue of the 23-vertex extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs.
targets.statement: : ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 25

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n5_tight
targets.plain: There exists a triangle-free graph on 25 vertices such that at least 25 edges must be removed to make it bipartite. The balanced blow-up of C_5 with five parts of size 5 witnesses this.
targets.statement: : ∃ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ ∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), H ≤ G → H.IsBipartite → 25 ≤ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

targets.name: Erdos23.blowupC5_tight
targets.plain: The blow-up of C_5 shows that the bound n^2 in Erdős Problem 23 is tight: any bipartite subgraph must omit at least n^2 edges.
targets.statement: (n : ℕ) (_hn : 0 < n) (H : SimpleGraph (ZMod 5 × Fin n)) (hH : H ≤ blowupC5 n) (hBip : H.IsBipartite) : n ^ 2 ≤ ((blowupC5 n).edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

targets.name: Erdos23.erdos_23
targets.plain: Can every triangle-free graph on 5n vertices be made bipartite by deleting at most n^2 edges?
targets.statement: : ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V], Fintype.card V = 5 * n → ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph V), H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ n^2

targets.plain: Are there only finitely many unitary perfect numbers?

targets.name: Erdos1052.even_of_isUnitaryPerfect
targets.plain: All unitary perfect numbers are even. Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.

targets.name: Erdos1059.erdos_1059
targets.plain: Are there infinitely many primes p such that p - k! is composite for each k such that 1 ≤ k! < p?

targets.name: Erdos1142.erdos_1142
targets.plain: Are there infinitely many n > 2 such that n - 2^k is prime for all k ≥ 1 with 2^k < n? The only known such n are 4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105 (OEIS [A039669](https://oeis.org/A039669)).

targets.name: Erdos1142.erdos_1142.variants.mientka_weitzenkamp
targets.plain: Mientka and Weitzenkamp [MiWe69] proved that the only n ≤ 2^44 such that n > 2 and n - 2^k is prime for all k ≥ 1 with 2^k < n are 4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105.

library.statement: (n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : d ∣ n
(n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : Nat.Coprime d (n / d)
(n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : d < n
(n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : d * (n / d) = n
(n d : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hd : d ∈ properUnitaryDivisors n) : Odd d
(n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n

steps.about: Every unitary perfect number is even. The route: write σ*(n) for the sum of all unitary divisors of n, n itself included. A unitary perfect n has σ*(n) = 2n. σ* is multiplicative, and σ*(p^k) = 1 + p^k. If n were odd, split off one prime power, n = p^k·m: then 2n = (1 + p^k)·σ*(m). Both factors are even when m > 1, so 4 divides 2n and n is even after all; when m = 1, 1 + p^k = 2p^k forces p^k = 1. Either way a contradiction.
steps.checked: With these steps taken as given, Lean accepts this route: the small steps prove S1 to S5, and S1 to S5 prove the target (shared-run/steps/1052.even_of_isUnitaryPerfect.lean). Every step is true: we proved each one privately before posting.

steps.plain: For n > 0, the unitary divisors of n are its proper unitary divisors plus n itself.
steps.statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : n.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (n / d)) = insert n (properUnitaryDivisors n)

steps.plain: n is not one of its own proper unitary divisors.
A unitary perfect number's unitary divisors, n itself included, add up to 2n.
steps.statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : IsUnitaryPerfect n) : ∑ d ∈ n.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (n / d)), d = 2 * n

steps.plain: A divisor of p^k other than 1 and p^k shares the factor p with its cofactor, so it is not a unitary divisor.
steps.statement: (p k d : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hd : d ∣ p ^ k) (h1 : d ≠ 1) (h2 : d ≠ p ^ k) : ¬ d.Coprime (p ^ k / d)

steps.plain: The unitary divisors of p^k (k ≥ 1) are exactly 1 and p^k.
steps.statement: (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hk : 0 < k) : (p ^ k).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (p ^ k / d)) = {1, p ^ k}

steps.plain: For a prime p and k ≥ 1, p^k is not 1.
steps.statement: (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hk : 0 < k) : (1 : ℕ) ≠ p ^ k

steps.plain: A prime power p^k (k ≥ 1) has exactly two unitary divisors, 1 and p^k.
steps.statement: (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hk : 0 < k) : ∑ d ∈ (p ^ k).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (p ^ k / d)), d = 1 + p ^ k

steps.plain: Every n > 1 has a prime divisor.
steps.statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n

steps.plain: The full power of p in n is coprime to the rest of n.
steps.statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hn : n ≠ 0) : (p ^ n.factorization p).Coprime (n / p ^ n.factorization p)

steps.plain: n is the full power of p in n times the rest.
steps.statement: (p n : ℕ) : p ^ n.factorization p * (n / p ^ n.factorization p) = n

steps.plain: A prime that divides n (n ≠ 0) appears in n at least once.
steps.statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hd : p ∣ n) : 0 < n.factorization p

steps.plain: Any n > 1 splits off one prime power: n = p^k·m with k ≥ 1 and p^k coprime to m.
steps.statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : ∃ p k m : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 0 < k ∧ (p ^ k).Coprime m ∧ n = p ^ k * m

steps.plain: For coprime a and b, a divisor d of ab is gcd(d, a) · gcd(d, b).
steps.statement: (a b d : ℕ) (h : a.Coprime b) (hd : d ∣ a * b) : d = Nat.gcd d a * Nat.gcd d b

steps.plain: For coprime a and b, a unitary divisor d of ab gives unitary divisors gcd(d, a) of a and gcd(d, b) of b.
steps.statement: (a b d : ℕ) (h : a.Coprime b) (hd : d ∈ (a * b).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a * b / d))) : Nat.gcd d a ∈ a.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a / d)) ∧ Nat.gcd d b ∈ b.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (b / d))

steps.plain: For coprime a and b, a unitary divisor of a times a unitary divisor of b is a unitary divisor of ab.
steps.statement: (a b x y : ℕ) (h : a.Coprime b) (hx : x ∈ a.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a / d))) (hy : y ∈ b.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (b / d))) : x * y ∈ (a * b).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a * b / d))

steps.plain: For coprime a and b, the unitary divisors of ab are the products x·y of a unitary divisor x of a and y of b.
steps.statement: (a b : ℕ) (h : a.Coprime b) : (a * b).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a * b / d)) = Finset.image (fun x : ℕ × ℕ => x.1 * x.2) (a.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a / d)) ×ˢ b.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (b / d)))

steps.plain: For coprime a and b, a divisor x of a and y of b are recovered from the product x·y.
steps.statement: (a b : ℕ) (h : a.Coprime b) : Set.InjOn (fun x : ℕ × ℕ => x.1 * x.2) ↑(a.divisors ×ˢ b.divisors)

steps.plain: The sum of unitary divisors is multiplicative: for coprime a and b, σ*(ab) = σ*(a)·σ*(b).
steps.statement: (a b : ℕ) (h : a.Coprime b) : ∑ d ∈ (a * b).divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a * b / d)), d = (∑ d ∈ a.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (a / d)), d) * (∑ d ∈ b.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (b / d)), d)

steps.plain: An odd number above 1 has an even sum of unitary divisors.
steps.statement: (m : ℕ) (hm : Odd m) (h1 : 1 < m) : Even (∑ d ∈ m.divisors.filter (fun d => d.Coprime (m / d)), d)
